sentences.text: Ankistrorhynchus is an extinct genus of sclerorhynchoid fish belonging to the class Chondrichthyes, which includes cartilaginous fish like sharks and rays.
This animal is placed within the family Sclerorhynchidae.
Scientists know this genus only from isolated rostral teeth found in two species.
The type species of the genus Ankistrorhynchus is A. lonzeensis.
This species was named after its type locality in Lonzée, Belgium.
The species A. major was named from fragmentary material found in New Jersey, USA, making its validity questionable.
The genus lived from the Santonian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 85.7 and 66 million years ago.
The species A. lonzeensis dates to the lower Santonian stage.
The species A. washakiensis was described from the Campanian-aged Mesaverde Formation in Wyoming, USA.
